verdict_rationale: The authors' script ran unmodified (byte-identical, one declared font-registration tolerance) and reproduced every value it produces: Fig. 3 (256/256), Table 2 (18/18), the S3 tables (2329/2329), and the Fig. 4 matrix and axis order exactly or within S3's storage precision; the named values all match. The departures are small and leave the conclusions unchanged: Table 1 differs in 8 of 130 cells by one type each, where the authors' own S3 supports the reproduction (PAPER_ERROR, escalated); 2 of 1176 GIMP-added box cells in Fig. 4 disagree with S1 (MINOR_DISCREPANCY); the Fig. 2 map aid lacks a basemap (MINOR_DISCREPANCY); and Fig. 5's motif-extent patches have no method (CANNOT_COMPARE, partial). Nearly all values reproduced and conclusions confirmed. Coverage 14/18: the four targets not credited remain in the denominator.

targets.evidence: comparisons/t01-fig2-bars.csv; map: visual comparison of outputs/run-05/files/captured/aid-T01-map.png with the published Fig. 2 map (comparison-report.md, T01)
targets.notes: Bar panel (authors' code, S2 Part 2): the 18 categories and their order are exact; every bar's chronology segments agree with the published bars to within one object, the measurement resolution of the published raster (3.2 px per object); reproduced counts sum to 483. Map panel (verification aid aid-T01, ggplot2 point plot of S1 Coord.Long/Coord.Lat by Chronology): 466 of 483 objects have coordinates (17 are recorded as '-' in S1); the spatial distribution and chronology colours match the published map (Ertebolle concentrated in Jutland, the Maglemose cluster on Zealand, Kongemose in Scania and Sweden, Kongemose/Ertebolle on the Polish coast). The aid has no basemap, projection, scale bar, or north arrow: per the plan's tolerance, differences caused only by unpublished conventions are MINOR_DISCREPANCY (ruling R1). Both panels passed their checks.

All 128 bars across the six panels: motif tuple and order identical (128/128), 4-decimal PMI label identical (128/128), bar total identical (128/128), and stacked chronology composition identical (128/128, a further 512 counts beyond the plan's 256). The Fig. 3b cut-off at 21 does not split a PMI tie (ranks 20-21 share 1.9584; rank 22 is 1.8807). Published bar totals and compositions were measured from the raster's pixels before the first run (published-values/README.md).

Matrix m (authors' code, S2 Part 7): 165 non-zero pair values; 163 agree with the S3 bigrams sheet to 15 significant digits and 2 (A24-ANT, I5-I13) differ by at most 5.3e-15, a rounding of the 15th digit by the authors' fwrite export (WITHIN_PRECISION under the plan's tolerance). Axis order: the 49 tokens are exactly the published order. Colour pattern: visual match. Small culture-exclusive boxes: 290 published boxes; the S1 lookup (aid-T03, all 1176 pairs of the 49 axis motifs) agrees on 289 cells; one published box differs in colour (C5-F13 is boxed yellow/Ertebolle, but its single bearing object is Kongemose in S1) and one exclusive pair has no box (B1-B2, a single Maglemose object). Both are single-object pairs that the heatmap does not plot (observed frequency < 3). The 290 boxes exceed the 165 plotted pairs, so the authors boxed culture-exclusive pairs at any frequency (criterion unpublished). The five large boxes (I5-I13; C4 C5 C12 C13 D7; D33-H1; B10-F38; A14-A24) all mark culture-exclusive pairs in the lookup; their PMI threshold is unpublished (visual). Box placement is therefore not exact (2 of 1176 cells), a small difference in GIMP-added annotations with conclusions unchanged; the remaining differences are GIMP styling (masked half, labels). Escalated for a ruling on whether the two cells are a paper error (evidence tier 2, the deposited S1) or a data-version effect.

targets.failure_mode: Fig. 5 motif-extent patches have no authors' code and no stated method, so they cannot be computed; only the pies and positions were verified (partial).
targets.notes: Pies (verification aid aid-T04, S1 lookup): all 10 objects' cluster-motif sets match the published pie colours exactly (10/10), and their positions agree with S1 coordinates (Spearman rank correlation 0.997 for x vs longitude, 1.000 for y vs latitude; numbering as Table 3). The coloured motif-extent patches have no code or stated method and cannot be compared, as the plan pre-declared, so the target is partially verified and counts against coverage (coverage-rules check scope).

Unigrams (31 rows) and quadrigrams (5 rows) match exactly, as do the four header totals (230, 1543, 4422, 8466). Eight cells differ by one type each: bigrams with frequency 8 (published 6, reproduced 5), 7 (8 vs 9), 4 (32 vs 31), 3 (59 vs 60), 2 (154 vs 153), and 1 (1224 vs 1225); trigrams with frequency 2 (222 vs 221) and 1 (4094 vs 4095). The authors' own deposited S3 bigrams sheet (evidence tier 2) has 5 bigrams at frequency 8, 9 at 7, 31 at 4, and 60 at 3, agreeing with the reproduction and not with Table 1; the frequency-1 and -2 cells are supported at tier 3 (the authors' code run unmodified on the authors' data). Table 1 is internally consistent (its columns sum to the stated n), so the paper's table and the authors' own deposit disagree. A likely but untested cause: the paper's methods cite Zenodo record 10623550, whose S1.xlsx differs from the version-of-record S1 (different md5 and size in the evidence pack); version 1 was not used, per AP-12. Conclusions unchanged. Escalated for human confirmation.

targets.method_deviation: The plan says to read the unigram frequencies from the authors' 'captured token_freqs'. That object exists only inside the authors' function ngramfunction() and is never a global object, so it cannot be captured without altering the authors' code. Decided during execution (2026-10-17, while writing the wrapper, before any comparison was made): the aid computes the same quantity with the documented quanteda calls ngramfunction() makes, colSums(dfm(tokens(corpus))) on the authors' corpus object, and cross-checks it against the authors' own global unigram-frequency object `freqs` (S2 Part 4, the Table 1 source). Both give the same top six. The planned source itself cannot be computed, so no separate planned-method result exists.

targets.notes: From the authors' Fig. 3b plot data (createResultTable output), cross-checked by the S1 lookup aid-T14 (the two agree on every bar): 0 Maglemose-exclusive, 1 Kongemose-exclusive (B10-F38), and 9 Ertebolle-exclusive bigrams. The stated count (nine) matches; the eight listed identities are all among them. The ninth, which the text omits from its list, is C5-C12 (PMI 2.1890). Scored against the stated values per ruling R4; the reproduction agrees with the stated count, so no PAPER_ERROR protocol applies. The list's omission is an internal inconsistency of the paper's text, resolved by the reproduction.
Among the ten culture-exclusive Fig. 3b bigrams (the approved scope), the highest total frequency is 5 (C4-C5).

Five motif identities confirmed (each appears in a plotted cluster pair); the six cluster pairs with observed frequency of 3 or more have PMI 2.19-3.29, agreeing with S3 to 15 significant digits (6/6) and appearing among the darkest cells of Fig. 4 (visual); all ten pairs co-occur only on Ertebolle objects in S1 (10/10). Four pairs (C4-C13, C4-D7, C12-D7, C13-D7) occur on fewer than 3 objects and are not plotted. Individually, C5 and C12 also occur on non-Ertebolle objects (C5: one Kongemose; C12: one Maglemose, one Kongemose), so the exclusivity holds for the combinations, as the plan's method tests it.

Verification aid aid-T17: exactly 10 S1 objects bear at least two of the five cluster motifs, and they are exactly the ten Table 3 objects (by Plonka figure). The inferred rule reproduces the printed 10 and the Table 3 set, so it is credited as the plan provides (ruling Q5).
S1 lookup of the ten Table 3 objects: 9 antler axes and 1 antler shaft (Ydernaes 6).
